theory.overview: Disjoint Set Union (DSU) or Union-Find is a data structure for tracking disjoint sets of elements. Supports two operations: find (determine which set an element belongs to) and union (merge two sets). With path compression and union by rank, operations are nearly $O(1)$ amortized. Used in Kruskal's MST, cycle detection, connected components, and dynamic connectivity. This chapter covers DSU structure, optimizations, and applications.

sections.title: DSU Structure
sections.content: Array parent where parent[i] = parent of element i (or i if root). Array rank for union by rank (tree height estimate). Initially, each element is its own set (parent[i] = i, rank[i] = 0). Find returns representative (root) of set. Union merges two sets by linking their roots.

structure.parent: parent[i] = parent of i (or i if root)

sections.title: Find Operation
sections.content: Find representative of element's set. Traverse parent pointers until root (parent[i] == i). With path compression: flatten tree by making each visited node point directly to root. Makes future finds faster. Time: $O(\alpha(n))$ amortized (inverse Ackermann function, practically constant).
sections.algorithm: def find(x): if parent[x] != x: parent[x] = find(parent[x]); return parent[x];

sections.title: Union Operation
sections.content: Merge two sets. Find roots of both elements. If same root, already in same set. Else, attach smaller tree under larger tree (union by rank). Update rank if heights equal. Time: $O(\alpha(n))$ amortized with path compression in find.
sections.algorithm: def union(x, y): px, py = find(x), find(y); if px == py: return; if rank[px] < rank[py]: parent[px] = py; elif rank[px] > rank[py]: parent[py] = px; else: parent[py] = px; rank[px] += 1;

sections.title: Optimizations
sections.content: Path compression: during find, make nodes point directly to root. Flattens tree structure. Union by rank: attach shorter tree under taller tree. Keeps trees shallow. Together, these ensure near-constant time. Without optimizations, operations can be $O(n)$ in worst case (degenerate tree).

sections.title: DSU Applications
sections.content: Kruskal's MST: detect cycles when adding edges. Connected components: count number of sets after processing all edges. Dynamic connectivity: answer if two nodes are connected. Percolation: model percolation in grids. Image processing: connected component labeling.

keyConcepts.name: Representative
keyConcepts.description: Root element that represents the set. All elements in set have same representative after find with path compression.

keyConcepts.name: Path Compression
keyConcepts.description: During find, make each visited node point directly to root. Flattens tree, ensures future finds are O(1).

keyConcepts.name: Union by Rank
keyConcepts.description: Attach smaller tree under larger tree's root. Keeps tree height O(log n) or better. Rank is upper bound on height.

keyConcepts.name: Inverse Ackermann
keyConcepts.description: $\alpha(n)$ grows extremely slowly (< 5 for all practical n). Makes DSU operations effectively constant time.

steps.title: Initialize DSU
steps.description: Create parent array where each element is its own parent. Initialize rank to 0.

steps.title: Find with Path Compression
steps.description: Find root, compress path by making nodes point directly to root.
steps.code: def find(x): if parent[x] != x: parent[x] = find(parent[x]); return parent[x];

steps.title: Union by Rank
steps.description: Find roots, attach smaller tree under larger. Update rank if equal.
steps.code: def union(x, y): px, py = find(x), find(y); if px == py: return; if rank[px] < rank[py]: parent[px] = py; elif rank[px] > rank[py]: parent[py] = px; else: parent[py] = px; rank[px] += 1;

steps.title: Check Connected
steps.description: Two elements are connected if find(x) == find(y).

steps.title: Count Components
steps.code: roots = set(find(i) for i in range(n)); return len(roots);

practiceProblems.title: Redundant Connection
practiceProblems.description: Find edge that can be removed to make tree (n nodes, n edges, one cycle).
practiceProblems.solution: Union-Find. Add edges one by one. If edge connects already connected components, it's redundant.

practiceProblems.title: Redundant Connection II
practiceProblems.description: Find edge to remove in graph with two possible cycles.
practiceProblems.solution: Union-Find with parent tracking. Handle cases: edge to same node, multiple parents.

practiceProblems.title: Number of Provinces
practiceProblems.description: Count number of connected components in matrix (1 = connected).
practiceProblems.solution: Union-Find on matrix. Union adjacent 1s. Count unique roots.

practiceProblems.title: Graph Valid Tree
practiceProblems.description: Check if graph is valid tree (n nodes, n-1 edges, connected, no cycles).
practiceProblems.solution: Check n-1 edges. Union-Find: if edge connects already connected components, cycle. Check if one component at end.
practiceProblems.hints: Union-Find, check n-1 edges and one component

practiceProblems.title: Accounts Merge
practiceProblems.description: Merge accounts with same email (each account has list of emails).
practiceProblems.solution: Union-Find on emails. Accounts with same email connected. Group by root.

practiceProblems.title: Sentence Similarity II
practiceProblems.description: Check if sentences are similar given similarity pairs (transitive).
practiceProblems.solution: Build graph from pairs. Union-Find on words. Check if each word pair connected.

practiceProblems.title: Satisfiability of Equality Equations
practiceProblems.description: Check if equality equations are satisfiable (a==b, b==c, a!=c → false).
practiceProblems.solution: Union-Find for equalities. For inequalities, check if variables in same component.

practiceProblems.title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
practiceProblems.description: Find longest consecutive elements sequence.
practiceProblems.solution: Hash set (not Union-Find). For each number, if num-1 not in set, it's sequence start.

practiceProblems.title: Making A Large Island
practiceProblems.description: Change one 0 to 1 to maximize island size in binary matrix.
practiceProblems.solution: DFS to label islands with sizes. Union-Find or DFS. For each 0, check adjacent islands.
practiceProblems.hints: Label islands with DFS, check each 0

practiceProblems.title: Most Stones Removed with Same Row or Column
practiceProblems.description: Find max stones that can be removed (stone removed if shares row/col with another).
practiceProblems.solution: Union-Find on rows and columns. Each connected component can have one stone left.

practiceProblems.title: Number of Operations to Make Network Connected
practiceProblems.description: Find minimum operations to connect all computers (can add cable between any two).
practiceProblems.solution: Count connected components. Need components - 1 cables. If cables < n-1, return -1.

practiceProblems.title: Bricks Falling When Hit
practiceProblems.description: Find bricks that fall after hitting a brick (connected to top = stable).
practiceProblems.solution: Union-Find with virtual top. Remove brick, check connectivity to top.

practiceProblems.title: Critical Connections in a Network
practiceProblems.description: Find critical connections (bridges) in network.
practiceProblems.solution: Tarjan's algorithm (not Union-Find). Track discovery and low times.

practiceProblems.title: Detect Cycles in Undirected Graph
practiceProblems.description: Detect cycle in undirected graph.
practiceProblems.solution: Union-Find. If edge connects already connected components, cycle exists.

practiceProblems.title: Detect Cycles in Directed Graph
practiceProblems.description: Detect cycle in directed graph.
practiceProblems.solution: DFS with 3 states (not Union-Find). Or Kahn's algorithm.

practiceProblems.title: Connecting Cities With Minimum Cost
practiceProblems.description: Find minimum cost to connect all cities (MST).
practiceProblems.solution: Kruskal's with Union-Find. Sort edges, add if connects different components.

practiceProblems.title: Optimize Water Distribution
practiceProblems.description: Minimize cost to provide water (pipes + wells).
practiceProblems.solution: Add virtual well node. Run MST on this graph.

practiceProblems.title: Min Cost to Connect All Points
practiceProblems.description: Find minimum cost to connect all points (complete graph, edge = distance).
practiceProblems.solution: Prim's (not Union-Find) or Kruskal's with Union-Find.

practiceProblems.title: Find Critical and Pseudo-Critical Edges
practiceProblems.description: Find edges that must be in all MSTs (critical) and edges in some MSTs (pseudo-critical).
practiceProblems.solution: For each edge, check if MST without it has same weight (pseudo-critical) or higher weight (critical).
practiceProblems.hints: Check each edge, compare MST weights

practiceProblems.title: Maximum Minimum Spanning Tree
practiceProblems.description: Find MST that maximizes minimum edge weight (bottleneck MST).
practiceProblems.solution: Kruskal's with Union-Find (same as regular MST, properties hold).

practiceProblems.title: Reorder Routes to Make All Paths Lead to City Zero
practiceProblems.description: Minimum edges to reverse so every node can reach node 0.
practiceProblems.solution: BFS from node 0 (not Union-Find). Count wrong-direction edges.

practiceProblems.title: Find the City With Smallest Neighbors
practiceProblems.description: Find city with smallest number of neighbors at distance threshold.
practiceProblems.solution: Dijkstra from each city (not Union-Find).

practiceProblems.title: Minimum Number of Vertices to Reach All Nodes
practiceProblems.description: Find minimum vertices to reach all nodes in directed graph.
practiceProblems.solution: Find SCCs (Kosaraju or Tarjan, not Union-Find). Count components with no incoming edges.

practiceProblems.title: Lexicographically Smallest Equivalent String
practiceProblems.description: Find lexicographically smallest string given equivalence pairs.
practiceProblems.solution: Union-Find on letters. For each position, find smallest equivalent letter.

practiceProblems.title: Remove Max Number of Edges to Keep Graph Fully Traversable
practiceProblems.description: Max edges to remove while keeping graph traversable (type 1 and type 2 edges).
practiceProblems.solution: Kruskal's with Union-Find for each type, count removable edges.
